journeyCxRedesign.note: Since the last checkpoint (outer loop complete, about to start jcx-s1's inner loop): /branch-setup, /implementation-plan, and implementation all ran for jcx-s1. The ORIGINAL implementation plan covered only the 3 backend-route tasks (AC1-AC4, NFR Security) -- AC5 (distinct placeholder render state) and the Accessibility NFR (keyboard-operable Add-placeholder/Trigger affordances) were missed, since the plan defaulted to 'this story is mostly backend' without re-checking each AC individually. Caught before /verify-completion by re-reading the story file; added as a documented Task 4 (CSS/markup + 2 new buttons + an inline form + click/submit handlers). While building Task 4, the new click handlers were first written assuming access to `list`/`reorderError`/`submitJson` -- locals that actually live in journeys.js's OWN SEPARATE stage-panel/reorder <script> IIFE, not the feature-picker IIFE this new code landed in (journeys.js renders 3 independent <script> blocks). Caught by running 3 pre-existing, unrelated test files directly (all three failed with 'list is not defined'); fixed by giving the new code its own local jcxList/jcxReorderError/jcxSubmitJson. /verify-completion's own mandatory live-browser render check could not be performed: the local dev server starts and logs 'listening on port 3000' (real Postgres, .env copied from the main checkout without reading its contents) but every HTTP request to it -- including a cold GET / before any of jcx-s1's own routes -- never completes (reproduced via both the Chrome extension's navigate and a plain curl; TCP reaches ESTABLISHED per netstat, but no HTTP response ever returns). Root cause unknown, not explained by this diff. Operator explicitly approved (via AskUserQuestion) substituting real jsdom dispatchEvent-driven E2E tests (including getComputedStyle visibility assertions, not mere DOM-presence) for the live-browser evidence. Draft PR #976 opened, then failed CI's 'Lint, typecheck, test, build' job -- the job log only prints failing FILE NAMES, no assertion detail, no log artifact uploaded -- so the real failure was reproduced in a Linux/Node 24 Docker container (matching the CI runner/Node version exactly) rather than guessed at. Root cause: the NFR path-traversal test's own `!fs.existsSync(scratchRoot/../../etc)` assertion resolves to the REAL, always-present /etc on Linux (os.tmpdir() is /tmp there), failing regardless of the guard -- it only passed on Windows by coincidence. The actual production guard (discovery-seeder.js's allowlist regex) was already correct, confirmed separately via the 400-response assertion. Fixed by narrowing the test to check for no artefacts/ dir under scratchRoot itself. Pushed, CI went green (all 8 checks), operator reviewed and merged PR #976 directly. Operator then reported being at their weekly usage limit -- this checkpoint is being written specifically to preserve state before that limit blocks further work. jcx-s1's own /definition-of-done has NOT yet been run (still required per CLAUDE.md even though the PR merged) -- this is the very next action for a future session, not jcx-s2.
